title: The New Climate Paradox, Imported From China
gist: A paywall-truncated piece argues that as of 2026 the two conditions long assumed necessary for the green transition — technical viability and price parity with fossil incumbents — have both been met, largely thanks to Chinese-made solar technology, yet frames this as producing a paradox rather than the expected decarbonization takeoff.

insights.claim: The conventional theory of the green energy transition held it would unfold once low-carbon technologies met two conditions: demonstrated technical viability versus incumbent carbon-intensive technologies, and 'price parity' with those established alternatives.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Lays out the standard two-condition framework analysts use to judge green-tech competitiveness, useful as a baseline for evaluating current claims about the energy transition's pace.
insights.quote: many have assumed that the green transition would unfold once two conditions were met

insights.claim: As of 2026, the article states both the technical-viability and price-parity conditions for green energy have been met, with more low-carbon energy technology available globally than ever before — yet frames this achievement as producing a 'paradox' rather than the expected acceleration in decarbonization.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Signals a disconnect between falling green-tech costs/performance and actual decarbonization outcomes worth investigating further — implies non-price barriers (e.g., trade policy, grid integration, geopolitics) are now the binding constraint on the energy transition.
insights.quote: As of 2026, both of these conditions have been met. In fact, there has never been a greater amount of green energy technology available globally
insights.locator: As of 2026, both of these conditions have been met

insights.claim: Chinese solar manufacturing, exemplified by plants such as Shanghai Shenzhou New Energy Development Co.'s facility in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, is central to the global supply of low-cost photovoltaic cells underpinning the price-parity claim.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
entities: Shanghai Shenzhou New Energy Development Co.
insights.so_what: Positions Chinese solar manufacturers as key price-setters for the global energy transition, relevant to assessing trade-policy risk (tariffs, anti-dumping measures) that could disrupt green-tech cost curves in importing countries.
insights.locator: A worker shows photovoltaic cells to be used to make solar panels

top_entities: Shanghai Shenzhou New Energy Development Co.
